concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a map is a top-view drawing of an area, small or large.
Distinguish physical, political and thematic maps and define an atlas.

topics.title: Distance and the scale of a map

concepts.learning_objective: State what a map's scale tells us about map and ground distances.
Calculate real distances from map measurements using a given scale.

topics.title: Direction and symbols on maps
topics.ncert_sections: A Map and Its Components (direction, symbols)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the cardinal and intermediate directions and use them on a map.
Explain why maps use standard symbols and who fixes them for India.

topics.title: Mapping the Earth: the globe and coordinates
topics.ncert_sections: Mapping the Earth; a) Understanding coordinates

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a globe represents the nearly spherical Earth better than a flat map.
Explain how two coordinates together fix a location precisely.
Describe parallels of latitude, the Equator and the poles and their values.
Relate latitude to torrid, temperate and frigid climates.
Describe meridians of longitude and how longitude is measured east and west.
Identify the Greenwich Prime Meridian as the 0 degree reference for longitude.
Describe the ancient Indian prime meridian through Ujjayini.
Relate the Earth's rotation of 15 degrees per hour to local time.
Calculate differences in local time from differences in longitude.

topics.title: Standard time, time zones and the International Date Line

concepts.learning_objective: Explain standard time and Indian Standard Time relative to GMT.
Explain why time zones follow borders and why large countries have several.
Explain the International Date Line and the change of date on crossing it.
